Jana (Acme): Hey team — we're seeing intermittent 400 errors from the embeddings endpoint when we batch requests. Example error: "400 Bad Request: dimension mismatch: expected 1536 got 1024". It happens about 1-2x / min during our peak (~2k req/min). No schema changes on our side. Using model=embed-v1 via the hosted API. Anyone seen this?

Alex (Support): Thanks Jana — can you paste a minimal repro and the exact request you used (headers + body)? Also any request-id from the error response would help.

Jana (Acme): Repro below. We call the bulk embeddings endpoint with an array of texts (20 items). We set max_batch_size=64 in our client config. Occasionally it returns the error for the whole request. Sample curl and error:

```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \n  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \n  -d '{"model":"embed-v1","input":["t1","t2",...,"t20"]}'
```

Response snippet: "{\"error\":\"dimension mismatch: expected 1536 got 1024\", \"request_id\":\"req_73a9f2f\"}"

Alex (Support): OK got request_id=req_73a9f2f. Sam / eng-runtime can you pull logs for that request_id and the time window around 1832104567?

Sam (eng-runtime): Looking now. I pulled the serving runtime trace for req_73a9f2f. Interesting — the batch that processed these items contained entries routed to two different model variants: `embed-v1` and `embed-v1-quant`. Our runtime has a batching path that assumed all items in a batch share the same output dim, but quantized variant returns 1024 dims. Partial log excerpt: 

```
2026-03-15T14:02:42Z [batch_worker] batch_id=b-19 size=20 models_seen={embed-v1:12, embed-v1-quant:8}
2026-03-15T14:02:42Z [kernel_selection] selected_kernel=fp16_attn kernel_shape=1536
2026-03-15T14:02:42Z [postproc] mismatch: expected_dim=1536 actual_dim=1024 -> raising DimensionMismatchError
2026-03-15T14:02:42Z [response] request_ids=[...], error=DimensionMismatchError, srv_req=req_73a9f2f
```

Sam (eng-runtime): It looks like dynamic routing/fallback can place requests for different model variants into the same micro-batch when under load. That's a bug in the batching logic — batches must be homogeneous along the (model_name, variant) key. Current code attempted to coalesce by shard only which allowed mixing.

Li (eng-ml): To add context — embed-v1 (full-precision) produces 1536-d embeddings; embed-v1-quant uses a lossy quantization/structure that returns 1024-d vectors (we compress axes, smaller final dim). Mixing them in the same batch will obviously break downstream concat/stack operations. This also explains the tail latency spike: when the batch mixing occurs we hit an exception path which stalls the worker until the error bubble propagates.

Alex (Support): Thanks Sam / Li. Jana — quick question: are you pinning a variant explicitly or relying on our auto-quantization fallback? (i.e., do you ever pass variant or let the service pick)

Jana (Acme): We only set `model=embed-v1`. We didn't set variant. We saw the fallback to quantized in the dashboard earlier (capacity policy "auto-quant" is enabled on our org). We assumed fallback would be transparent.

Nora (PM): Noted. For customers that call a specific model name we should ensure that fallback doesn't silently change the output schema. That seems like a dangerous UX.

Sam (eng-runtime): Short-term mitigation options:
- Customer side: pin to full-precision variant explicitly (e.g., `model: "embed-v1@full"`) or set a header `X-Prefer-Full-Precision: true` (we can accept this now for hosted)
- Customer side: set `max_batch_size` to smaller value (e.g., 1 or 8) to reduce chance of mixed batches (workaround)
- Server side hotfix: enforce homogeneous batching by (model, variant) key and split mixed batches instead of coalescing. I'll push a small change to split batches and return a clear 409 if mixing requested variants is attempted.

Temporary client repro snippet (Python) that triggers the error when auto-quant is on: 

```python
# naive batched call that sometimes fails under load
from redwood import RedwoodClient
rc = RedwoodClient(api_key=...)
texts = ["hello"] * 20
rc.embeddings.create(model="embed-v1", input=texts, max_batch_size=64)
```

Li (eng-ml): Also recommending: platform should disallow variant substitution that changes embedding dimensionality for the same model alias. If fallback to quantized is necessary for capacity, we should either:
1) preserve dim (quantize with same output dim) OR
2) return an explicit response telling the client we used a different model/embedding-dim, so client can handle it.

Sam (eng-runtime): Action plan:
- Hotfix (<= 2h): batching split by (model_name, variant) and return 409 with helpful message if a mixed batch was previously attempted. This avoids the dim-mismatch crash and makes errors deterministic.
- Followup (3-7 days): routing change so fallback chooses a compatible variant (matching dim) or a transparent upcasting strategy.

Alex (Support): Jana, I'll propose these two immediate workarounds: pin the variant or set max_batch_size=1 while we roll the hotfix. Which would you prefer?

Jana (Acme): We'll flip to `max_batch_size=1` for now (we can tolerate the cost hit) and pin later. Please let us know when hotfix is deployed.

Sam (eng-runtime): Starting hotfix deployment now. Spawning canary with split-by-variant change.

infra-bot: deploy triggered by sam/eng-runtime for service=runtime-batcher, deploy_id=deploy_20260315_01

deploy-bot: canary passed (node-3), rolling to 20% traffic

Sam (eng-runtime): Canary looks clean, splitting batches by (model_name,variant) fixed the crash in our local repro tests. Rolling patch to prod.

deploy-bot: rollout complete: service=runtime-batcher version=2026.3.15_hotfix_01

Alex (Support): Jana — hotfix deployed and should prevent the dimension-mismatch crash. Please re-enable your normal batch size and monitor; let us know if you still see errors.

Jana (Acme): Thanks, I can confirm errors stopped after we reverted to normal batch size (observed for 30m). We'll keep an eye and will pin variant for safety. Really appreciate the quick turnaround :thumbsup:

Sam (eng-runtime): Follow-up: we'll add an alert for mixed-variant batch attempts and a dashboard metric so we can proactively detect this class of issue.

Li (eng-ml): I'll own the longer-term change to guarantee embedding-dim compatibility across fallback variants (or fail fast with clear metadata when incompatible).

Nora (PM): Filing a short post-incident note and updating docs to recommend explicitly pinning variants if customers rely on fixed-dim outputs.

Alex (Support): Closing the loop with Jana and leaving thread open for any residual questions. Thanks everyone.
